label: GO step, confident a2 choice after a common transition, before trial ~75
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass) and only when the agent chooses a2 (99.96% of active steps have action==2; model_act==2 at every active step). Within that it needs a strongly negative policy logit (choice < -6 covers 99.7% of mass), and it is essentially silent when the previous trial had a rare transition (rate 0.005 vs 0.066 after common) or the previous choice was a1. It also depends strongly on time in the episode: rate rises from about 0.05 to 0.08 over trials 10-69, then drops to near zero after trial ~75 and is never active in trials 90-99. Nothing at D1 or D2, never when in_rew==1 or when a state/action input is present. Magnitude: largest on the first one or two GO steps of a run of common a2 choices, then decaying over consecutive repeats (e.g. 0.6, 1.0, 0.47, or 0.81, 0.46, 0.14, 0.03 in the top windows). The predicate is observed-only: choice is the model's own GO logit, not a future variable. Using action==2 instead of the logit (with prev_action!=1) gives F1 0.65. Precision is about 0.53 because many confident a2 GO steps late in long a2 streaks stay inactive, which fits the decay-within-streak magnitude pattern. I could not capture that with a simple streak-position predicate.
